title: China Airlines 140
time_reference: JST (local, UTC+9); t0 is the GO lever activation at about 20:14, the exact second is not reproduced

agencies.name: Aircraft Accident Investigation Commission
agencies.report_title: Aircraft Accident Investigation Report, China Airlines, Airbus Industrie A300B4-622R, B1816, Nagoya Airport, April 26, 1994

summary: On final approach to Nagoya the first officer inadvertently triggered the go-around (GO) lever, putting the autothrottle and flight director into go-around mode. The crew tried to continue the approach by pushing the nose down while the autopilot, engaged in go-around mode, trimmed the horizontal stabiliser fully nose-up against them. When the captain took over and added power the out-of-trim aircraft pitched up steeply, stalled at about 1,800 ft and fell onto the airport. Of 271 on board, 264 died.
probable_cause: The AAIC concluded that the accident resulted from the first officer's inadvertent activation of the GO lever, the crew's continued attempt to land while the autopilot was in go-around mode, and the resulting out-of-trim condition in which the trimmable horizontal stabiliser moved to its nose-up limit while the elevators were held nose-down. The captain's late takeover and the application of go-around thrust then produced a pitch-up beyond the crew's ability to control, leading to a stall. Contributing factors included the flight control computer design, under which the autopilot could not be overridden by control-column force in go-around mode, the fact that an Airbus service bulletin correcting this had not been incorporated, inadequate crew training on the autopilot's go-around behaviour, and deficient crew coordination.

factors.evidence: The first officer, as pilot flying, inadvertently activated the GO lever on final approach at about 1,070 ft, and later held the control column forward against the autopilot.
The crew did not fully understand that the autothrottle, flight director and then the autopilot were in go-around mode and continued trying to land.
The AAIC found the crew had not been adequately trained in the autopilot's behaviour in go-around mode and in the recovery from an out-of-trim condition.
In go-around mode the A300-600 autopilot could not be disengaged by force on the control column, and the automatic trim moved the stabiliser opposite to the pilots' elevator input.

Airbus had issued a service bulletin to modify the flight control computers so that the autopilot would disconnect with control-column force in go-around mode, but it was not mandatory and its urgency was not conveyed.
The service bulletin had not been incorporated on B-1816, and a similar earlier incident had not led to corrective action.
With the stabiliser trimmed to the nose-up limit, the elevators lacked the authority to counter the pitch-up when thrust was increased.
The captain's instructions to the first officer were not effective, the takeover of control was late, and neither pilot monitored the trim state.
The crew were dealing with unexpected autoflight behaviour at low altitude in the final phase of the approach.
The aircraft pitched up to over 50 degrees, lost airspeed and stalled at about 1,800 ft.
The aircraft fell tail-first onto the airport grass east of the runway.

events.text: Before the accident: Airbus service bulletin A300-22-6021, modifying the flight control computers so that control-column force disengages the autopilot in go-around mode, is available but not mandatory; it has not been incorporated on B-1816.
Night ILS approach to Nagoya runway 34; the first officer is pilot flying, the captain is pilot monitoring.
At about 1,070 ft the first officer inadvertently triggers the GO lever; the autothrottle enters go-around mode and thrust increases, and the flight director commands go-around.

The captain tells the first officer to disengage the go-around mode and continue the approach; the first officer reduces thrust manually and pushes the control column forward, but the flight director remains in go-around mode.

The autopilots are engaged while go-around mode is active. The autopilot commands nose-up while the first officer holds the column forward; the automatic trim runs the horizontal stabiliser toward the nose-up limit while the elevators are nose-down.
The stabiliser reaches its full nose-up position; the aircraft is severely out of trim, and the pilots are unaware of the trim state.
The angle of attack increases and alpha-floor protection commands go-around thrust, adding to the pitch-up tendency.
The captain takes control and decides to go around, increasing thrust; with full nose-up trim and high thrust the aircraft pitches up steeply despite forward elevator.
Pitch attitude exceeds 50 degrees and airspeed decays rapidly; the aircraft stalls at about 1,800 ft.
The aircraft falls tail-first onto the grass east of runway 34 and breaks up in flames; 264 of the 271 on board are killed, 7 survive.

recommendations.to: Ministry of Transport (Japan) / DGAC France / Airbus
recommendations.text: Make mandatory the flight control computer modification allowing the autopilot to be disengaged by control-column force in go-around mode, and review the design so that the autopilot cannot trim against sustained pilot input.
recommendations.outcome: The DGAC issued an airworthiness directive mandating the service bulletin on A300-600 and A310 aircraft.

recommendations.text: Improve crew training on autoflight mode awareness, the go-around mode behaviour of the autopilot, out-of-trim recovery and crew coordination.

safety_changes: The Airbus flight control computer modification for A300-600 and A310 aircraft was made mandatory by airworthiness directive.
Operators reinforced training on autoflight mode awareness and recovery from out-of-trim conditions.
China Airlines undertook a review of its training and operating procedures under pressure from regulators.

notes: Only the impact time (20:15:45 JST) is given as a clock string; event offsets are approximate and t0 is the GO lever activation at about 20:14.
The stabiliser trim reached the nose-up limit (about -12.3 degrees); the exact value is omitted from the state fields.
The service bulletin number is given as A300-22-6021 from memory and should be verified.
The report date (July 1996) and report number (96-5) are from memory.
